chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from 'Abbad ibn Sulayman, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, who said:

I asked him about a man who performed Zuhr or 'Asr, then breaks his wudu (ablution) when he sits in the fourth [rak'ah]. He said: If he had said, "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah," then he does not repeat [the prayer]. But if he had not recited the tashahhud before breaking his wudu (ablution), then he must repeat.

key_terms.أَشْهَدُ: I bear witness; the opening wording of the testimony in tashahhud
key_terms.الرَّابِعَةِ: the fourth rak'ah of the salat (prayer)
key_terms.فَلْيُعِدْ: then he must repeat the salat (prayer)
key_terms.فَيُحْدِثُ: he breaks ritual purity by an occurrence nullifying wudu (ablution)
key_terms.يَتَشَهَّدْ: to recite the tashahhud in prayer

ai.seo_question: If someone breaks wudu in the fourth rak'ah of Zuhr or 'Asr after tashahhud, must the prayer be repeated?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding one who breaks wudu (ablution) while seated in the fourth rak'ah of Zuhr or 'Asr. If he had already recited the testimony of tashahhud, the salat (prayer) is not to be repeated; otherwise, it must be repeated.
